blocks.content: This topic ties DaemonSet, Job, and CronJob together, three genuinely different workload shapes, each solving a distinct problem that Deployments and StatefulSets, covered in earlier modules, simply do not fit.

Each of this module's workload types is defined by a different answer to "what triggers this Pod to run": a DaemonSet is triggered by node existence, a Job is triggered once, manually or programmatically, a CronJob is triggered on a recurring schedule.

blocks.alt: Three genuinely different answers to what actually triggers a Pod to run

blocks.content: As covered in its own topic, a DaemonSet's Pods exist because a node exists, one per node, continuously, for as long as that node is part of the cluster, the right fit for node-level infrastructure.

blocks.alt: Running continuously, tied directly to node existence

blocks.content: A Job runs once, to completion, and then stops, the right fit for a genuinely one-off task, a migration, a data processing run, anything with a clear beginning and end.

blocks.alt: A clear beginning and a clear end, run exactly once

blocks.content: A CronJob is a Job triggered repeatedly, on a schedule, the right fit for anything that needs to happen regularly, nightly backups, periodic cleanup tasks, scheduled reports, without anyone manually re-triggering it each time.

blocks.alt: A Job, repeated automatically, exactly on the schedule you define

blocks.content: 5. The Contrast With Deployment and StatefulSet
blocks.text: 5. The Contrast With Deployment and StatefulSet

blocks.content: Every workload type covered in earlier modules, Deployment and StatefulSet, is built around long-running, replica-count-based Pods, always up, self-healing indefinitely, the three types in this module exist precisely for the cases that shape does not fit at all.

blocks.alt: A genuinely different shape, for genuinely different needs than the earlier modules covered

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: DaemonSet, Job, and CronJob each answer a different question about what triggers a Pod to run: node existence, a one-time trigger, or a recurring schedule.
These fill the gap Deployment and StatefulSet, both built around long-running replicas, deliberately do not address, choose based on what actually triggers the work.
